correctness.rationale: The published pointwise index is applied only to the appropriate nonzero interval-diagonal maps. For signed offset h, each rank r has 2(n-h-r+1) placements; threshold summation yields T_n(t) exactly. This gives the harmonic limit via a uniform integral comparison. The mean is a weighted divisor sum, and the Dirichlet hyperbola bound proves the stated sharp additive constant. Fixed-h Riemann sums with a summable h-tail prove the second-moment coefficient; finite-h convergence proves macroscopic tails. Sparse-map composition in verify.py independently checks all integer index counts for 2<=n<=12; it checks arithmetic moment sums beyond. Numerical checks are not treated as asymptotic proof. The zero map is excluded throughout.

value.rationale: The nilpotency depth is an intrinsic power invariant of a published, naturally defined finite inverse-monoid family. A complete exact distribution and its heavy-tailed limit exhibit an infinite limiting mean but logarithmically growing finite means with a sharp constant; rare depths of order n generate variance asymptotic to pi^2*n/12. These interacting scales and the macroscopic-tail profile are nontrivial structural information, not a one-parameter recoding or a small numerical table.
